data.cultural_impact: The name 'Surya' or 'Sūraj' holds a significant cultural impact in Indian society and Hindu mythology. In Hinduism, the Sun God, Surya, is one of the most important deities and is worshipped as a symbol of power, energy, and creation. This reverence towards the Sun God can be seen through various aspects of Indian culture, including rituals, festivals, and traditions. For instance, people wake up early to greet the sun and offer prayers to it, and there are various festivals such as Makar Sankranti and Navratri that honor the Sun God. The significance of the Sun God can also be seen in various art forms, including sculptures, paintings, and poetry.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Sūraj' carries deep meaning and significance. The Sun God is believed to represent the divine light that illuminates the world and infuses it with life and energy. He is also considered a symbol of consciousness and awareness, with the ability to dispel darkness and ignorance. The worship of the Sun God is believed to bring blessings of health, wealth, and prosperity, and to help one overcome challenges and obstacles. The name 'Sūraj' itself is a reminder of the divine power within us, and the potential we have to tap into this power and transform ourselves and our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Sūraj represents the radiant and powerful sun god, who is the giver of light and life. It symbolizes vitality, energy, and the ability to inspire warmth and joy in others.

historical_references.reference: The god Surya or Sūrya, also called Aditya, is considered one of the Adityas, the 'sun gods' in Hinduism. Surya is the deity of the sun and presides over all the celestial bodies. According to the Rigveda (circa 1500-1200 BCE), Surya is described as a red-glowing god, the lord of the day and the driver of the chariots of the sun. He is also the god of kings and rulers.

Another reference to Sūrja is found in the Mahabharata (circa 400 BCE). In this epic, Surya is considered the father of Yama, the god of death, and is invoked by the character Bhishma during his final moments. Bhishma requests Surya to grant him a boon to choose the time of his death and to be remembered as a warrior who lay on a bed of arrows for sixty days.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'सूरज' (Surya) in modern context is widely used in various domains including Astrology, Spirituality, and Renewable Energy. In Astrology, it is the name of the Sun deity, and many people consult astrologers to know about their Sun sign and its impact on their personality. In Spirituality, 'Surya Namaskar' (Sun Salutations) is a popular practice in yoga, paying homage to the Sun god. In Renewable Energy, 'Solar Energy' is a growing trend inspired by the Sun, which provides the energy required for various applications. The name 'सूरज' (Surya) is also seen on Instagram through hashtags and posts related to these topics. It is discussed on WhatsApp groups dedicated to Astrology, Spirituality, and Renewable Energy. On LinkedIn, professionals can find 'Surya' as a name in various profiles, especially for those working in the fields of Astrology, Spirituality, and Renewable Energy.
